VBO:0200922.summary: Lively, alert and adaptable in its breed standard, the ash-colored Mudi shares the working character of the other colors. Hungarian shepherds use Mudis with large and difficult livestock, and the standard also records their use in wild-boar drives. Their independently turning ears give the watchful farm dog a distinctive expression.
VBO:0200922.shortDescription: An ash-colored Hungarian Mudi, sharing the breed standard’s lively, alert character and livestock-working tradition.

sources.title: Mudi: Official FCI Breed Standard (2023)
sources.evidence: Whole2023 FCI238 specifies lively/courageous/watchful/keen-to-work/alert/adaptable and able to learn, herding large/difficult livestock and wild-boar battue/watch-alarm uses. Ears independently turning are literal. Named Ash(Blue), Liver(Brown), Fawn(BeigeToRed), White coat forms and corresponding nose pigment rules support exact morphology. Character applies to breed generally; color does not cause different temperament.

VBO:0200925.summary: Lively and watchful in the breed standard, Mudis are keen workers with a capacity for learning. Hungarian shepherds use them to herd large, difficult livestock, drawing on the breed’s courageous disposition. Their ears can turn independently. Brown is a coat form of this same working breed, with no separate character assigned to its color.
VBO:0200925.shortDescription: A brown-coated Hungarian Mudi, sharing the breed standard’s lively, watchful character and work with difficult livestock.

VBO:0200926.summary: Keen to learn and ready for work in its breed standard, the fawn Mudi shares the breed’s lively, courageous character. Hungarian shepherds use Mudis to move large and difficult livestock; watch and alarm work is also documented. Their ears can turn independently, an expressive detail of an alert herding dog.
VBO:0200926.shortDescription: A fawn Hungarian Mudi, sharing the breed standard’s lively character, readiness to learn and livestock-working tradition.

VBO:0200927.summary: Alert, lively and watchful in its breed standard, the white Mudi shares its working character with the other coat forms. This Hungarian herder is used with large and difficult livestock and in wild-boar drives. Its ears can turn independently, a distinctive expression of the responsive farm dog described by the standard.
